references.text: Describes how the Lord struck Sihon and Og, kings of the Amorites and Bashan, and gave their land to Israel - this is the land that Gad and Reuben refer to as 'the land the Lord has struck'.
The context explaining that the children of Reuben and Gad had large herds, and the land was well suited for livestock.
Moses recounts the victory over Sihon, king of Heshbon, whom the Lord gave into Israel's hand.
Moses recounts the victory over Og, king of Bashan, and the distribution of the land to Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh.
Confirms that Moses gave land east of the Jordan to Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh after the Lord had struck the kings there.
The victory over the Midianites, which was part of the conquests 'before the assembly of Israel'.
Describes the Israelites' background as shepherds with livestock (מִקְנֶה), explaining why land suitable for grazing was important to them.
